PRINCIPLE: The management overview should show WHAT WE ARE WORKING ON (semantic intent), not WHAT TOOL IS BEING CALLED (mechanical action). 'Editing WorkerPanel.tsx' is secondary noise. The focus/intent is primary.

SOURCE: Ned explicitly corrected Claude mid-session when it stripped the focus field and replaced it with tool summaries: 'Did I ask for the latest tool action? The goal is to have an overview of what the fuck is happening.'

APPLICATION: Panel hierarchy — focus text (bright, primary) → tool action (dimmed, secondary). Never strip the focus field. Never make tool names the headline. The semantic meaning of what Claude is doing trumps the mechanical action it's taking.
